segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Let's look at this week's escalations. We had seven, which is up from four last week.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Three of them are the same root cause, the CSV export timing out for accounts with more than fifty thousand rows.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Engineering has a fix in review. They're moving the export to a background job with an email link.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay. Ravi, can you draft a macro for the agents so customers know a fix is coming?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yes, I'll have it up in an hour.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The fourth escalation was the clinic group that got double-billed. Finance already issued the refund.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I called their office manager yesterday. She was gracious about it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Speaking of calls, Elena, how did your date go Saturday? The guy from the climbing gym?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Oh god. He spent forty minutes talking about his ex and then asked if I wanted to split a cab back to his place. Hard no.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Stop. Are you going to see him at the gym now?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I'm switching to the Tuesday class, which is a shame because the Thursday instructor is way better.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay, okay. Back to the list. The last three are one-offs?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yes. A login loop on an old Safari version, a webhook misconfiguration on the customer side, and one feature request that got escalated by mistake.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Let's close the feature request and route it to product. Anything else?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Just that weekend coverage is thin next month, I'll post the schedule for volunteers.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Thanks both. Same time next week.
